Meet @seanlyles. NYC vinyl DJ, model, and a man on a mission to revive the art of dancing. All while looking good in the new Grid Cord collection.

I think of The Fitness Marshall as a superhero alter ego. He’s someone who can be happy, fearless, and bursting with energy on command. \
\
That joy is a very real part of me- but so is the self-doubt, the anxiety, the grief I carry for the little boy who grew up thinking something was so terribly wrong with him.\
\
I often see comments making fun of how flamboyant\/feminine\/gay I am. I don’t feel embarrassed or hurt by that anymore. I feel so grateful that I no longer have to hide. I feel so lucky that I get to be exactly who I am and feel comfortable and proud of that person. \
\
Being gay is a core piece of my identity because it shapes how I experience and navigate the world.\
\
I won’t ever dim my light for someone else’s comfort again, and I hope you don’t either.\
\
Love who you love. Be who you are.\
\
The people who truly care about you will still be there, even if it takes time. \
\
And thank you, @chubbies for giving me the opportunity to be loud, proud, and GAY on your socials outside of June :) 🏳️‍🌈🏳️‍⚧️
Gamedays start in the tunnel.

SMALL PEOPLE, BIG ADVENTURES\
\
As parents, we wish to protect our children, to keep them safe from harm, yet risk is inherent in life. But when you learn to recognize the dangers, you figure out ways to manage the risks. And exposure to hardship and risk-taking allows kids to build self confidence and become more resilient, equipping them to better navigate future challenges.\
\
When our daughter Freya was 11 and our son Jackson was 8, we embarked as a family on a year of adventures. It felt like the right timing, before the pressure of their next chapter begins. But this was by no means a year-long vacation; the adventures were tough and uncomfortable, and the kids continued their schooling throughout. But it was an opportunity to spend quality time as a family away from the hustle of our busy lives, and get out of our Western bubble.\
\
Children are far more capable than most realise. Given the opportunity they can accomplish extraordinary things. This is our three-part film series capturing our family taking risks, embracing discomfort, and experiencing the world together. – Leo Houlding, Professional Climber & YETI Ambassador \
\

Hosting a Halloween party at home or at school? Make it one every kid can enjoy with these tips from a few of the allergy parents on team Partake who’ve been there. 🎃 \
\
#kidsparty #allergyfriendly #halloween

The Monster Mash has never been so delicious! 👻🍫\
\
These Spooky Chocolate Covered Monsters start with @partakefoods mini grahams pressed into a sprinkle-covered milk chocolate base, then get dressed up in colorful white chocolate, googly eyes, and goofy grins. \
\
No baking required, and every monster turns out one of a kind!\
\
How to make 12: \
1️⃣ Melt milk chocolate + 1 tsp coconut oil in 30-second bursts. Spread on a baking mat. \
2️⃣ Sprinkle with sprinkles. \
3️⃣ Press Partake mini grahams into the chocolate in even rows. \
4️⃣ Melt white chocolate + 1 tsp coconut oil, pour into squeeze bottles, and tint your monster colors. \
5️⃣ Coat the grahams, add candy eyes, and draw on mouths. \
6️⃣ Chill until set, break apart, and enjoy!\
\
Share this with someone who’s 100% in the Halloween spirit. \
\
Full recipe at the link in bio.\

Spot a teal pumpkin this Halloween? 🎃 It means that house has non-food treats, so kids with food allergies can trick-or-treat, too.\
\
Want to be a teal pumpkin house? It takes 3 steps:\
1️⃣ Add your home to the Teal Pumpkin Project map\
2️⃣ Put out a teal pumpkin or a free printable sign\
3️⃣ Stock up on non-food treats like glow sticks, stickers and spider rings\
\
Swipe for treat ideas and how it all started, then share this with friends who plan to hand out candy. 💜\
\
Our full guide, with links to FARE’s free resources, is on our blog at the link in bio.\
\
